title: Engineering Thermodynamics
objectives: Apply the first and second laws of thermodynamics to closed and open systems; evaluate properties of pure substances; analyse basic power and refrigeration cycles.
syllabus_text: Basic concepts: system, boundary, state, process, cycle. Zeroth law and temperature. Work and heat interactions. First law for closed systems and control volumes. Properties of pure substances; steam tables; quality. Second law; Carnot cycle; entropy; isentropic efficiency. Availability and irreversibility. Introduction to vapour power cycles and vapour compression refrigeration.

title: Fluid Mechanics
objectives: Analyse fluids at rest and in motion; apply control volume forms of mass, momentum and energy; estimate losses in internal flows.
syllabus_text: Fluid properties and viscosity. Fluid statics, manometry, hydrostatic forces on surfaces, buoyancy. Kinematics of flow; streamlines; continuity. Integral relations: mass, momentum, energy. Bernoulli equation and its limitations. Dimensional analysis and similitude. Internal flows: laminar and turbulent pipe flow, friction factor, minor losses. Introduction to boundary layers and drag.

title: Heat Transfer
objectives: Formulate and solve conduction problems; estimate convective coefficients; size simple heat exchangers.
syllabus_text: Modes of heat transfer. Steady one-dimensional conduction in plane walls, cylinders and spheres; composite walls; critical radius of insulation. Fins and extended surfaces. Transient conduction; lumped capacitance; Biot and Fourier numbers. Forced and natural convection; dimensionless groups; empirical correlations. Radiation: black and grey surfaces, view factors. Heat exchangers: LMTD and effectiveness-NTU methods.

title: Mechanics of Materials
objectives: Determine stresses and deflections in bars, shafts and beams; apply failure theories to component design.
syllabus_text: Stress and strain; Hooke's law; elastic constants. Axially loaded members; thermal stresses. Torsion of circular shafts. Shear force and bending moment diagrams. Pure bending; flexure formula; shear stresses in beams. Deflection of beams. Transformation of stress; principal stresses; Mohr's circle. Thin and thick cylinders. Columns and buckling. Theories of failure.

title: Manufacturing Processes
objectives: Select appropriate primary and secondary manufacturing routes; explain process capability and defects.
syllabus_text: Casting: patterns, moulding sands, gating and risering, solidification, casting defects. Metal forming: rolling, forging, extrusion, drawing, sheet metal operations. Joining: arc and resistance welding processes, weld defects, brazing and soldering. Machining: mechanics of metal cutting, tool materials, tool wear, turning, milling, drilling, grinding. Introduction to additive manufacturing and process selection.

title: Design of Machine Elements
objectives: Design shafts, fasteners, springs and bearings against static and fatigue loading.
syllabus_text: Design philosophy and standards. Static and fatigue failure; S-N curves; stress concentration; Soderberg and Goodman criteria. Design of shafts and keys. Threaded fasteners and bolted joints. Welded joints. Springs. Rolling and sliding contact bearings. Gears: terminology, force analysis, strength and wear considerations. Clutches and brakes.
